# tiny-worktree

> Zero-dependency git worktree management for parallel AI agents. One branch, one checkout, one command.

Zero runtime dependencies. Requires Python 3.8+ and git on PATH.

## Install

    pip install git+https://github.com/hussain-alsaibai/tiny-worktree.git

Not on PyPI: the name "tiny-worktree" belongs to another project.

## Python API

    from tiny_worktree import (
        new_worktree, list_worktrees, remove_worktree, worktree_path,
    )

    wt = new_worktree("feat/issue-42")   # -> <repo>-worktrees/feat-issue-42
    wt.path, wt.branch, wt.head
    list_worktrees()                      # every worktree, main one included
    remove_worktree(wt)                   # refuses to lose uncommitted work
    worktree_path(repo, "feat/issue-42")  # the path a branch would get

Classes: Worktree (path, branch, head, detached, locked, prunable, name,
exists(), to_dict()), WorktreeError.

Functions: new_worktree, list_worktrees, remove_worktree, worktree_path,
prune_worktrees.

## CLI

    tiny-worktree new <branch>          create; prints the path
    tiny-worktree new <branch> --base <ref>
    tiny-worktree list                   name + path for every worktree
    tiny-worktree path <branch>          print the path it would get
    tiny-worktree rm <branch>            remove it
    tiny-worktree exec <branch> <cmd>    run a command inside it
    tiny-worktree prune                  clean up stale admin entries

Add --json to new, list or prune for machine-readable output.

## Guarantees

- Paths are deterministic: same repo + same branch -> same path, always.
- Branch names are sanitized; a branch can never resolve outside the
  worktrees directory.
- remove_worktree refuses to discard uncommitted changes without force=True.
- prune_worktrees(dry_run=True) passes git's -n and really does not change
  anything.
- Every failure raises WorktreeError with git's own message attached.

## Tests

38 tests. The suite runs against real throwaway git repositories, not mocks.
Passes on Python 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12.
